newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cbank to evaluate rates after econ measures.
newsitem.headline: Czech cbank to evaluate rates after econ measures.

text.p: The Czech National Bank (CNB) will re-evaluate monetary policy after it has digested a government announcement on moves to boost the economy, due later Wednesday, CNB governor Josef Tosovsky was quoted as saying.
"The CNB is waiting to see which measures to resolve the current account deficit the government will take," Czech business daily Hospodarske Noviny quoted Tosovsky as saying.
"And according to this it (the CNB) will again look at the whole monetary situation and decide whether it is necessary or not to make any corrections to monetary policy," he added.

The government is due to announce at around 1300 GMT a package of measures designed to stimulate flagging growth and cut the country's spiralling trade deficit. The current account for 1996 leaped to 4.5 billion dollars from 1.6 billion the previous year.
So far, officials have been tight lipped about their plans but the Czech crown has fallen sharply on fears that the government wants a weaker currency to boost exports.

However, on Tuesday Tosovsky appeared to rule out a devaluation of the crown as part of the government's new measures and at the weekend central bank board member Jan Vit told Reuters that no cut in interest rates was imminent.
The crown has fallen in recent days to as low as 2.5 percent below the mid-point of its mark/dollar fixing basket from around 1.7 percent above the mid-point just one week ago.
On Wednesday morning, the crown was trading around 30.5 to the dollar and 17.6 to the mark implying a deviation from the basket of -0.8 percent.
